messages.text: we have a 5 month old. would we qualify for WIC? we make about $4200 a month together

Congratulations on your baby! I can check this for you. I need a couple of details first:

1. Who lives in your home and shares food? Is it you, your partner, and the baby, or are there others? Please give everyone's age.
2. Is the baby's mom breastfeeding? Is the $4,200 a month before taxes?
me (30), my husband (32), and the baby. just the three of us. yes I'm breastfeeding. and yep, $4,200 is before taxes

**WIC looks likely for you and your baby.**

**What to do next**
- Call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942) or go to a local health department clinic. The website is https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html.
- At the clinic, you'll have a short health and nutrition check.

**Why**
- WIC serves babies under 1. It also serves moms who are breastfeeding, up to a year after birth. You and your baby both fit. (Source: [7 CFR 246.2, WIC definitions](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2))
- For a household of 3, the WIC limit is $4,212 a month before taxes. Your $4,200 is just under it. (Source: [USDA's WIC income guidelines, July 2026 to June 2027](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926))
- You're very close to the limit. A raise, overtime, or other income could put you over, so bring recent pay stubs.

**Other programs I checked**
- **TennCare/CoverKids: likely for your baby.** Babies under 1 can qualify up to $4,440 a month for a family of 3. It looks unlikely for you and your husband, because the parent limit is $2,277. Apply at https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or call 855-259-0701. (Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))
- **Food assistance (SNAP): unlikely.** Your income after deductions is about $3,143, and the limit is $2,277. You can still apply at https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application or call 866-311-4287. I didn't have your rent, utility, or child care costs. Those could lower the countable income, but probably not by enough. (Source: [USDA's FY 2027 SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola))

For free local help applying, you can dial 211.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply.
